prompt: Recommend movies to a user based on what similar users rated highly.
tells: based on what similar users rated highly
why: Use the user–item ratings matrix to find similar tastes.
trap: Clustering users is coarser than learning each user's preferences.

prompt: Show "customers who bought this also bought" on product pages.
tells: customers who bought this also bought
why: Item-to-item collaborative filtering from co-purchase data.
trap: No product attributes are needed, only behavior.

prompt: You have 2 million users and 500,000 songs, but each user has played under 0.01% of the songs.
why: Matrix factorization learns low-dimensional user and item vectors from sparse interactions.
trap: Standard PCA struggles with mostly-missing data; factorization is built for it.

prompt: A recommender works well for long-time users but shows random items to new users who have no history.
tells: new users who have no history
why: The cold-start weakness of collaborative filtering: fall back to popularity or content features until history builds.
trap: Bandits can help explore, but the issue to name is CF's need for history.
